settings.legal.privacy.uninstall_body: Removing PlxNative removes the application, but webOS gives an application no way to run code as it is removed, so anything kept outside the application’s own directory can survive. Your sign-in is deliberately kept there so that reinstalling does not sign you out. Your optional-reporting answers and their Crash report ID and Analytics ID are kept with that sign-in, so that a decision you have already made is not put to you again after a reinstall. Your app language preference is also kept there. Use Delete all local data BEFORE uninstalling if you want nothing of PlxNative left on this television.

settings.consent.preview.crash_intro: Crashes / Errors — what is actually sent to Sentry in Germany, and only when error reporting is on. Random and build-specific values are placeholders; fixed classes below are representative values from the closed domains in the Privacy notice. Nothing else is sent. The crash report identifier is random, is created only when crash reports are enabled, and is shown here as a placeholder.
settings.consent.preview.usage_intro: Analytics / Usage — what is actually sent to PostHog in Germany, and only when usage reporting is on, with a random Analytics ID. Random and build-specific values are placeholders; fixed classes below are representative values from the closed domains in the Privacy notice. Nothing else is sent. The usage identifier is random and is created only when product analytics is enabled.

settings.consent.analytics.absent:
NO ANALYTICS ID

Product analytics is off, so this installation has no analytics identifier and is sending no analytics events.

An identifier is created only when you turn product analytics on, and deleting it is what turning it off does. If you had analytics on before and want events from that period deleted, write to {contact} — but note that the identifier they carry was destroyed when analytics was turned off, so it can no longer be looked up from this television.

Crash reports do not use this identifier. They carry a separate Crash report ID, shown on its own row while crash reports are on.
settings.consent.analytics.present:
YOUR ANALYTICS ID

{id}

WHAT IT IS

A random identifier created on this television when you turned product analytics on. It is attached to analytics events so they can be counted as coming from one Analytics ID: one uninterrupted opt-in on one television. It is not derived from your Plex account, your television or anything about you, and it is never sent with crash reports, which carry a separate Crash report ID of their own.

HOW TO HAVE THESE EVENTS DELETED

Write to {contact} and quote the identifier above. It is the only handle these events carry, so a request without it cannot be matched to anything.

HOW IT ENDS

Turning product analytics off deletes this identifier, and turning analytics on again creates a different one. Signing out removes it as well, and the next person to sign in is asked afresh; so does Delete all local data. Events already sent keep the old identifier, which is why it is worth copying down before you turn analytics off if you intend to ask for their deletion.
settings.consent.errors.absent:
NO CRASH REPORT ID

Crash reports are off, so this installation has no crash report identifier and is sending no crash or error reports.

An identifier is created only when you turn crash reports on, and deleting it is what turning them off does. If you had crash reports on before and want reports from that period deleted, write to {contact} — but note that the identifier they carry was destroyed when crash reports were turned off, so it can no longer be looked up from this television.
settings.consent.errors.present:
YOUR CRASH REPORT ID

{id}

WHAT IT IS

A random identifier created on this television when you turned crash reports on. It is attached to every crash and error report so that repeated crashes under one Crash report ID are counted once, which is what tells a problem that hit many people apart from one television that hit it many times. It is not derived from your Plex account, your television or anything about you, and it is never sent with product analytics, which has a separate Analytics ID of its own.

HOW TO HAVE THESE REPORTS DELETED

Write to {contact} and quote the identifier above. It is the only handle these reports carry, so a request without it cannot be matched to anything.

HOW IT ENDS

Turning crash reports off deletes this identifier, and turning them on again creates a different one. Signing out removes it as well, and the next person to sign in is asked afresh; so does Delete all local data. Reports already sent keep the old identifier, which is why it is worth copying down before you turn crash reports off if you intend to ask for their deletion.

settings.playback.force_body:
Bypasses playback compatibility checks and always uses original quality. Playback may have no sound, display incorrectly, freeze, or crash the app. PlxNative will not automatically switch to compatible playback and may not recover gracefully.

Enable this only if you understand these risks and know how to restart the app and return Direct Play to Auto.
settings.playback.force_note: Advanced override. Playback may fail or crash; automatic fallback is off. Return to Auto if problems occur.
settings.audio.account_note: Saved to this Plex profile and shared with your other Plex apps. Changes may take time to affect playback; selections already made for an item still take priority.
settings.playback.copy: Playback defaults for this television. Changes here apply to the next playback.
settings.playback.quality.copy: The highest quality a video plays at. Larger files are converted by your Plex server to fit. Also available in the player's More menu.
settings.playback.direct_play.copy: Auto plays the original file when this television can; otherwise your Plex server converts it. Disabled always converts. Force skips every check: for troubleshooting only.
settings.playback.subtitle_size.copy: How large subtitle text is. Picture and styled subtitles keep their own size. Also under Style in the player's Subtitles menu.
settings.playback.subtitle_position.copy: How high subtitles sit on the picture. Picture and styled subtitles keep their own position. Also under Style in the player's Subtitles menu.
settings.playback.next_episode.copy: Up Next countdown shows a Next episode button when the credits start. After credits lets them play, then starts the next episode. Off closes the player instead.
